item.title: NPS chief draws line between investing, politics

item.title: US tariffs hit Hyundai Motor Q4 profit
item.description: Hyundai Motor said Thursday its fourth-quarter operating profit fell 40 percent from a year earlier as higher US tariffs weighed on earnings, overshadowing gains from improved pricing and favorable exchange rates. Operating profit for the October-December period fell 39.9 percent on-year to 1.69 trillion won ($1.19 billion), while revenue edged up 0.5 percent to 46.84 trillion won. item.title: SK hynix doubles down on HBM to cement unrivaled market lead
item.description: SK hynix expressed confidence Thursday in capturing an overwhelming share of the HBM4 market, replicating its dominance in earlier generations of high bandwidth memory that has been all-important to artificial intelligence, after posting record profit in 2025. During an earnings call, the chipmaker also said it will ramp up capital expenditure this year to meet explosive growth in AI memory demand. item.title: Korea to add 60,000 homes in Greater Seoul area
item.description: South Korea on Thursday unveiled a plan to add about 60,000 new homes in Seoul and the broader capital area, seeking to cool an overheated housing market by expanding supply in prime locations. Under the roadmap, the government will supply 60,000 housing units targeted at young people and newlyweds across Seoul, Gyeonggi Province and Incheon, covering a total area of 4.87 million square meters. item.title: Olive Young brings 'K-wellness' into focus with Olive Better
item.description: CJ Olive Young has become a living catalog of the ever-expanding world of K-beauty. It is now seeking to extend that formula to wellness, this time in a separate store format. Named Olive Better, Olive Young’s first wellness-curation store opens Friday, as the beauty retailer tries to turn a sprawling post-pandemic wellness boom into something more concrete and legible. item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Thursday that US President Donald Trump's remarks on potential tariff hikes aimed at South Korea do not amount to a rupture of an existing trade agreement, framing it instead as part of ongoing discussions over the implementation. item.title: GS25 sees 74% surge in foreign payments
item.description: GS Retail said Thursday that payments made by foreign visitors at its convenience store chain GS25 jumped 74.2 percent year on year in 2025, reflecting a strong recovery in inbound tourism. Mobile payment services led the increase, with Alipay and WeChat Pay accounting for 97.7 percent of all foreign transactions, underscoring the rapid shift toward cashless spending among overseas visitors, particularly from Asia. item.title: What the crackdown on 'cyber wreckers' mean
item.description: Two recent court rulings have cast a spotlight on South Korean YouTube channels that profit from sensationalized or fabricated content while harming reputations and private lives. item.title: Sejong University to launch international summer program
item.description: Sejong University said Thursday it will launch a four-week international summer program for outstanding undergraduate students from around the world starting this year. The university announced that the Sejong International Summer Program will run from June 29 to July 24, aligning with Sejong University’s summer semester.
